title: KernelProtocol
description:
One root type that references every wire type, so a single schema file carries them
all under `$defs`.

Backoff.description: How the delay grows between attempts.

oneOf.description: Every retry waits `initial_ms`.
The delay is `initial_ms * factor^(attempt - 1)`, capped at `max_ms`.

Cause.description: Failure taxonomy. Retry policy is keyed on this, never on application error text.

oneOf.description: The attempt exceeded its wall-clock budget (`timeout_ms`). Retryable.
The worker stopped heartbeating and its lease expired. Retryable.
The activity threw. Retryable.
The user cancelled the run. Never retried.
The worker's output failed schema validation. Never retried.
A re-fold diverged from the journal. Never retried.
Dispatch an activity to a worker; opens a `task` step in `scheduled`.

activity.description: Activity name the worker dispatches on.

retry.description: Retry policy; the default policy when `None`.

timeout_ms.description:
Wall-clock budget for one attempt. The worker aborts at it; the host's backstop
reaps the attempt if the worker never answers.

oneOf.description: Open a `timer` step that fires at an absolute or relative time.

fire_at_ms.description: Absolute fire time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. One of the two is required.

fire_in_ms.description: Delay in milliseconds from the event's `ts_ms`; ignored when `fire_at_ms` is set.

oneOf.description: Start a child run; opens a `child` step in `scheduled`.
Park on a named signal; opens a `signal` step in `awaiting_signal`.

timeout_ms.description: Wait budget in milliseconds; `None` waits forever.

oneOf.description: Publish to a side channel. Never journaled, never replayed.
End the run as `completed`. Must be the last command of the reduction.

End the run as `continued` and start a successor with `input`. Must be the last
command of the reduction.

ContinueAsNew.description: Input for the successor run when the reducer issued `continue_as_new`.

child_run_id.description: `run_` followed by the first 26 hex chars of `sha256(task_id)`.

Envelope.description:
A journaled event: `EventInput` plus the kernel-assigned sequence number and the
state hash after folding it (so a re-fold can pinpoint the divergent seq).

attempt.description:
Task attempt this event is about (1-based); a `retrying` event names the *next*
attempt. `0` for every other kind.

error.description: Free-text error detail for `failed` task events. Never interpreted by the kernel.

kind.description: Event kind; the kernel routes on `kind`, `status` and `step_id`.

parent_run_id.description: The parent run, when this run was spawned as a child.

parent_step_id.description: The parent's `spawn` step, when this run was spawned as a child.

payload.description: Inline JSON payload, byte-exact. Exactly one of `payload` / `payload_ref` may be set.

random.description: 32 lowercase hex chars of host-generated randomness, journaled for replay.

run_id.description: The run this event belongs to.

schema_ref.description: Schema the payload conforms to (`<name>@<content-hash>`), when known.

seq.description:
Sequence number assigned by the journal writer; strictly increasing per run,
starting at `1`.

state_hash.description:
Hash of `(kernel_state, state)` after the transition that produced this event
(see `docs/kernel-protocol.md`).

status.description: The step status this event moves the step to.

step_id.description: The step this event belongs to; `start` for the `started` marker.

ts_ms.description:
Host wall-clock at submission, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. The reducer's
only clock.

usage.description: Resources this event consumed; banked into `KernelState::usage_total`.

EventInput.description:
An event as the host submits it, before the kernel assigns `seq` and `state_hash`.

`random` is 32 hex chars of host-generated randomness, journaled so that every
consumer of randomness (retry jitter, reducer `random`) is replay-stable.

attempt.description:
Task attempt this event is about (1-based); a `retrying` event names the *next*
attempt. `0` for every other kind.

error.description: Free-text error detail for `failed` task events. Never interpreted by the kernel.

kind.description: Event kind; the kernel routes on `kind`, `status` and `step_id`.

payload.description: Inline JSON payload, byte-exact. Exactly one of `payload` / `payload_ref` may be set.

random.description: 32 lowercase hex chars of host-generated randomness, journaled for replay.

run_id.description: The run this event belongs to.

schema_ref.description: Schema the payload conforms to (`<name>@<content-hash>`), when known.

status.description: The step status this event moves the step to.

step_id.description: The step this event belongs to; `start` for the `started` marker.

ts_ms.description:
Host wall-clock at submission, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. The reducer's
only clock.

usage.description: Resources this event consumed; banked into `KernelState::usage_total`.

HashAtSeq.description: A `(seq, state_hash)` pair, from the journal or from a re-fold.

Jitter.description: Randomization applied to the computed delay.

oneOf.description: Use the computed delay as-is.

Full jitter: scale the delay by a uniform fraction taken from `random`, so the
result lies in `[0, delay]`.

KernelError.description:
A kernel failure. `code` is one of the closed set the kernel defines; the host
branches on it, never on `message`.

message.description: Human-readable detail. Not stable; never branch on it.

seq.description: The seq the failure concerns, when it concerns one.

step_id.description: The step the failure concerns, when it concerns one.

KernelState.description:
Kernel-owned state persisted beside the user's state and included in the state hash.
Terminal steps are pruned deterministically (`closed_steps` keeps the count) so the
structure stays bounded on long runs.

closed_steps.description: Number of steps pruned from `steps` so far.

status.description: Run-level status as the kernel derives it from the open steps.

step_no.description: Monotonic counter used to derive default step ids.

steps.description: Open steps keyed by step id. Terminal steps are removed, not kept.

usage_total.description: Usage banked across every event of the run, retried attempts included.

v.description: Format version of this structure; currently `1`.

features.description: Feature names the host may branch on. Additive only.

protocol.description: Protocol version; the host refuses a kernel whose value differs from its own.

Kind.description: The five event kinds. Projects cannot add kinds (see `docs/kernel-protocol.md`).

oneOf.description: An activity executed by a worker.
A durable timer the host fires at `fire_at_ms`.
An external signal delivered to a parked `await_signal` step.
A child run spawned by this run.
Kernel bookkeeping: `start`, `cancel`, `fail`, `complete`, `continue`, `nondeterminism`.

step_id.description: The parent's step that owns the child.

NewTask.description: A task row to insert. It doubles as the outbox entry the host pushes to a worker.

activity.description: Activity name the worker dispatches on.

lease_ttl_ms.description: Lease duration in milliseconds before the reaper may re-dispatch.

queue.description: Queue the task is pushed to.

retry.description: Retry policy resolved for this task.

schema_ref.description: Input schema reference, when the reducer named one.

step_id.description: The step that owns the task.

timeout_ms.description: Per-attempt wall-clock budget in milliseconds; `None` means no budget.

fire_at_ms.description: Absolute fire time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

step_id.description: The step that owns the timer.

cause.description: Why it failed. Non-retryable causes always yield `retry: false`.

policy.description: Policy of the step that failed.

random.description: Journaled randomness (32 hex chars); the only entropy source for jitter.

run.description: The run row as loaded under the run lock.

state.description:
The current user-state checkpoint, byte-exact. Lifecycle transitions echo it and
hash it without calling the reducer, so the host must pass it for any event that
is not `started`.

Prepared.description: Output of `prepare_event`: what the host does next.

oneOf.description:
Call the reducer. For `started`, `init_input` is set: call `init(input)` first,
then `on.started`.

init_input.description: Workflow input for `init`; set only for `started`.

kernel_state.description: The kernel state to pass back into `reduce_step` (fresh for `started`).

reducer_event.description: The event to hand to the reducer.

oneOf.description:
Pure bookkeeping (task `running`, `retrying`, `cancelled`, …). No reducer call;
apply the transition as-is. `state` in it echoes the current checkpoint.

event.description: The trigger event, as passed to `prepare_event`.

run.description: The run row as loaded under the run lock.

ReducerEvent.description:
What the reducer sees. The kernel translates journal headers into these; the
reducer never sees `seq`, `random` or lifecycle noise except where it needs them.

`usage_total` rides on every variant: it is the run's banked total *including* this
event, so a reducer can decide on a budget without keeping its own tally
(see `docs/workflows.md`).

oneOf.description: The run's first event, delivered right after `init(input)`.

random.description: 32 hex chars of journaled randomness; the reducer's only entropy.

ts_ms.description: Event time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; the reducer's clock.

usage_total.description: Banked usage for the run, including this event.

oneOf.description: A task reached `succeeded` or `failed`.

activity.description: Activity name recorded on the step.

random.description: 32 hex chars of journaled randomness; the reducer's only entropy.

ts_ms.description: Event time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; the reducer's clock.

usage.description: What this attempt itself consumed; zeroed when the worker reported none.

usage_total.description: Banked usage for the run, including this event.

oneOf.description: A signal was delivered to a parked step.

name.description: Signal name recorded on the step.

payload.description: Signal payload; JSON `null` when the event carried none.

random.description: 32 hex chars of journaled randomness; the reducer's only entropy.

ts_ms.description: Event time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; the reducer's clock.

usage_total.description: Banked usage for the run, including this event.

oneOf.description: A timer fired.

random.description: 32 hex chars of journaled randomness; the reducer's only entropy.

ts_ms.description: Event time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; the reducer's clock.

usage_total.description: Banked usage for the run, including this event.

oneOf.description: A child run reached a terminal status.

output.description: Child output, when the event carried a payload.

random.description: 32 hex chars of journaled randomness; the reducer's only entropy.

ts_ms.description: Event time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; the reducer's clock.

usage_total.description: Banked usage for the run, including this event.

Reduction.description: What the reducer returned: the new user state (byte-exact JSON) and its commands.

actual.description: Hashes the re-fold produced, ascending by seq.

expected.description: Hashes as journaled, ascending by seq.

RefoldCheckOutput.description: `matches: false` carries the first divergent seq and both hashes.

actual.description: Re-folded hash at `seq`; empty when the re-fold produced none.

expected.description: Journaled hash at `seq`; empty when the journal has no entry there.

RetryPlan.description: `retry: false` means the step fails for good; `next_attempt` / `delay_ms` are set iff `retry`.

delay_ms.description: Delay before that attempt, in milliseconds.

RetryPolicy.description:
Declared per activity in the schema registry (see `docs/workflows.md`). Integers only
so the policy can live inside the hashed `KernelState`.

max_attempts.description: Total attempts including the first. `1` means never retry.

RunPatch.description: The run-row columns a transition rewrites.

last_seq.description: New `last_seq`: the seq of the last event in `Transition::events`.

RunRef.description: The run row as the host loaded it under the per-run lock.

bundle_digest.description: Content digest of the workflow bundle the run is pinned to.

last_seq.description: Seq of the last journaled event; `0` before `started`.

parent_run_id.description: The parent run, when this run was spawned as a child.

parent_step_id.description: The parent's `spawn` step, when this run was spawned as a child.

oneOf.description: Row exists, `started` not yet folded (child runs and continue-as-new go through the outbox).
`started` folded; steps may be open.
Every open step is a signal wait: nothing progresses until a signal arrives.
Terminal: the reducer issued `complete`.
Terminal: the reducer threw, nondeterminism was detected, or the host failed the run.
Terminal: the user cancelled the run.
Terminal: the reducer issued `continue_as_new`; a successor run carries on.

SignalWait.description: An open `await_signal` step the host registers so a matching signal can be delivered.

expires_at_ms.description: Absolute expiry in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; `None` waits forever.

schema_ref.description: Payload schema reference, when the reducer named one.

oneOf.description: Opened, not yet accepted by a worker (timers, children and markers start here too).
A worker accepted the task.
Terminal: the step produced a result.
Terminal: non-retryable cause, attempts exhausted, or `schema_violation`.
A retry was planned; the step returns to `scheduled` for the next attempt.
Terminal: cancelled by the run or by the user.
Parked until a signal is delivered.

StepState.description: Kernel bookkeeping for one open step.

attempt.description: Current attempt (1-based for tasks, `0` for every other kind).

fire_at_ms.description: Fire time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch (timers only).

TaskUpdate.description: A status change on an existing task row.

attempt.description: The attempt the update applies to.

not_before_ms.description: For `retrying → scheduled`: the earliest dispatch time.

Transition.description:
The write-set. Journals apply it atomically under the run lock and never interpret
commands themselves (see `docs/journal.md`).

completion.description: Set when the run ended in this transition.

continue_as_new.description: Set when the run continues as a successor run.

events.description: Trigger event first, then lifecycle `scheduled` events for each new task/timer/spawn/wait.

state.description: User state, byte-exact JSON. Stored inline when `state_inline`, else offloaded.

task_updates.description: Status changes to existing task rows.

Usage.description:
Resource usage stamped on events and summed into `KernelState`. Integers only,
because `KernelState` is hashed.

cost_micro_usd.description: Cost in micro-USD (1 USD = 1_000_000). Integer so the hash stays float-free.

normalized.description: The event after validation; currently a byte-exact copy of the input.
